parsed.summary: Three of the four candidates are now evaluated or rejected. LiNbF6 (mp-aaacjjwh) is the leading acceptable option: bin-1 penalty 0.0288, insulating with a 4.79 eV gap, cathode W_adh about 3.62 J/m2, and electrolyte W_adh about 1.63 J/m2 as the weaker contact. LiTaF6 (mp-aaacjmqp) is a close second: bin-1 penalty 0.0271, insulating with a 5.92 eV gap, cathode W_adh about 3.34 J/m2, and electrolyte W_adh about 1.58 J/m2 (registry range 1.53 to 1.58). Its penalty is marginally lower, but adhesion favours LiNbF6 on both contacts, so LiNbF6 ranks first. LiCaAlF6 (mp-aaaaajby) is acceptable and insulating with a 7.64 eV gap, but its penalty is bin 2 (0.0477) and its adhesion is weak: cathode about 1.43 J/m2 and electrolyte about 0.74 J/m2 at the selected registry, with the electrolyte registry range spanning 0.52 to 0.74. It is dominated by both bin-1 fluorides and ranks third. LiF (mp-aaaaabru) is thermodynamically rejected (penalty 0.31, bin 15) and stays last regardless of adhesion. Recommended next step: take LiNbF6 forward, with LiTaF6 as the backup. Before relying on the LiCaAlF6 electrolyte number, check how min_W_adh is defined, because the reported value appears to be the selected-registry value rather than the lowest registry value.
parsed.prior_prediction_assessment: HELD: (1) The initial penalty-only ordering (LiTaF6, then LiCaAlF6, then LiF) matched the penalty bins and acceptance flags. (2) The LiTaF6 prediction held. Predicted cathode W_adh [3.2, 3.9] contained the validated 3.34 J/m2. Predicted electrolyte W_adh [1.4, 1.9] contained 1.58 J/m2, and the lower registry value 1.53 also fell inside. The electrolyte was correctly identified as the weaker contact. Penalty bin 1 and acceptance were unchanged on evaluation, and the revisit triggers did not fire. The fluoride-analogue pattern from LiNbF6 transferred. FAILED: (3) The implicit preference for LiTaF6 as the leading coating did not survive adhesion data. LiNbF6 has higher adhesion on both contacts (electrolyte 1.63 vs 1.58; cathode 3.62 vs 3.34) for a penalty difference of only about 0.002, so LiNbF6 should rank first. (4) The LiCaAlF6 prediction failed. Predicted cathode [3.0, 3.8] and electrolyte [1.4, 1.9] both missed badly: cathode about 1.43 and electrolyte about 0.74 J/m2. The electrolyte-as-weaker-contact call was correct, but the magnitudes were not, and the electrolyte fell below the 1.4 J/m2 trigger that was set to reconsider the bin-2 choice. The prediction that LiCaAlF6 could be promoted on adhesion was not supported. UNRESOLVED: (5) The LiCaAlF6 electrolyte robustness case (seed-4 bulk) was not run because no admissible construction exists, and its thickness increment was not run (1,302 atoms exceeds the 1,250 limit), so the wide electrolyte registry spread cannot be tightened.
